traditional.text: And I say also unto thee, That thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.

ait.text: And I in turn tell you: you are Peter, and on this rock I will build my assembly, and the gates of Hades will not overpower it.

explanation: The Greek *ekklēsia* was the word for a gathering of citizens, and in the Greek Old Testament for Israel assembled before God. "Church" now suggests a building or an institution. The same verse keeps *Hades*, the realm of the dead, where older versions have "hell".

traditional.text: Therefore when thou doest thine alms, do not sound a trumpet before thee, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and in the streets, that they may have glory of men. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward.

ait.text: So when you give to the needy, do not sound a trumpet ahead of you, as the performers do in the synagogues and in the streets, so that people will praise them. Truly I tell you, they have been paid their reward in full.

explanation: In Matthew 6 the charge is religion staged for an audience, and the Greek word began as the term for a stage actor. Elsewhere, where the charge is pretense, this translation keeps "hypocrites": by the first century the word already meant that too. "Paid in full" is the wording of receipts from the period.

traditional.text: The light of the body is the eye: if therefore thine eye be single, thy whole body shall be full of light.

ait.text: The lamp of the body is the eye. So if your eye is generous, your whole body will be full of light;

explanation: The saying sits between treasure in heaven and serving wealth, and the "evil eye" that follows was a Jewish idiom for stinginess. Most translations keep the physical image with "healthy" or "sound"; this one follows the idiom and says so in the note.

traditional.text: And saying, The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God is at hand: repent ye, and believe the gospel.

ait.text: and saying, “The time has been fulfilled, and the kingdom of God has come near. Turn back, and believe in the good news.”

explanation: "Repent" now centres on feeling sorry. The Greek carries the prophets' call to return to God: a change of direction. Most translations keep "repent" as an established term.

traditional.text: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.

ait.text: In the beginning was the Logos, and the Logos was with God, and the Logos was God.

explanation: Left untranslated because "the Word" is now commonly heard as meaning the Bible. The note at this verse gives both backgrounds: God's creating speech in Genesis, which most scholars see as primary and which "Word" reflects, and the Greek sense of reason and order.
